title: Domain-specific biochemical and serological characterization of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein
protocol: Thaw purified protein on ice.
Filter DLS buffer with a 0.22 μm filter.
Dilute protein solution into 2 mg/mL.
Prepare 120 μL of sample for each protein, sufficient for technical triplicates.
Add 35 μL of sample to each well in a Corning® Low Volume 384-well Clear Flat Bottom plate.
Centrifuge sample for 5 min at 4°C using a tabletop centrifuge at top speed to remove aggregates.
Check for presence of dust in wells before loading.
Cover plate with aluminum foil whenever possible when not loading to reduce likelihood of dirt getting inside.
Place pipette tip on the bottom of well and pipet slowly while loading.
Avoid generating bubbles during loading.
Gently shake plates if bubbles are trapped inside and remove bubbles by pipetting.
Set up experiment for acquisition.
Set correlation function high cutoff to 60 ms.
Acquire well images set to Yes.
Set DLS Acq time to 5 s.
Set DLS Number Acq to 10.
Set Auto-attenuation time limits to 60 s.
Access Regularization Graph and use triplicates to reach consensus when analyzing data.
Remove peaks with less than 1% mass.
Align triplicates to check consistency for each major peak.
Determine statistics of measured radius across triplicates.
Determine the highest concentration point for the protein titration series.
Create a 2.5 fold dilution series with 12 concentration points starting from 10 μM as the highest concentration.
Prepare 120 μL of the highest concentration point.
Pipette 90 μL binding buffer into each of 11 Eppendorf tubes.
Mix 60 μL from the highest concentration tube into the next concentration point.
Repeat mixing to complete the entire dilution series.
Calculate the amount of RNA needed for each duplicate run.
Prepare 700 μL of labeled RNA stock at 2 nM (resulting in a final concentration of 1 nM after mixing with protein).
Cover tubes with aluminum foil to protect from light.
Load the protein dilution series into wells of a 96 well plate, placing each titration series in one row.
Load 25 μL of RNA into each well.
Load buffer and RNA only controls in row C.
Read with Cytation 5 Cell Imaging Multi-mode Reader.
Set excitation to 485 nm and emission to 528 nm with a bandpass of 20 nm.
Set read height to 8.5 mm.
Determine FP values using Gen5 Analysis software.
Fit KD using Origin.
Calculate averages and standard deviations for titration points in Excel.
Fit binding curves using Origin.
Repeat each experiment containing duplicates at least three times.
Report statistics about KD values across technical repeats.
Place glow-discharged carbon-coated copper grids onto a glass slide with the carbon film side facing up.
Put the glass slide on the sample stage of Leica EM ACE600.
Glow discharge for 45 seconds with settings: Current (12 mA), Air (2.0E-1 mbar), Working Distance (50 mm), and Tilt (0°C).
Apply 2 μL of sample at 1 mg/mL diluted in PBS to each grid.
Wait for 1 minute.
Blot the grid with filter paper for 3 seconds.
Place grids on parafilm and wash with three droplets of ddH2O, each containing 20 μl.
Stain grids with two droplets of 2% uranyl acetate solution, each containing 20 μl.
Air dry the stained grids before imaging with an electron microscope.
Prepare fresh 2% UA from 4% UA stock solution.
Spin the prepared solution for 1 minute at top speed using a tabletop centrifuge.
Face the grid onto a ddH2O droplet to wash for 30 seconds.
Blot the grid for 3 seconds after washing.
Repeat the ddH2O washing step two more times.
Repeat the washing with 2% UA two more times.
Airdry the grid before storing in a grid box.
Image grids using an electron microscope.
Load each negative-stained grid onto the side-entry holder of JEOL JEM-1400plus Transmission Electron Microscope operating at 120 kV.
Record images with AMT XR111 high-speed 4K × 2K pixel phosphor-scintillated 12-bit CCD camera at magnifications between 3,000 to 40,000.
Coat recombinant N proteins on a 96 well flat bottom immunosorbent plate at a concentration of 500 ng/mL in 100 μL coating buffer.
Incubate the coated plates overnight at 4°C for 12-18 hours.
Rinse the plates with 150 μL wash buffer (PBS with 0.1% Tween-20).
Dilute plasma samples 1:100 in dilution buffer (PBS with 0.05% Tween-20 and 0.1% FBS) for a total volume of 200 μL.
Incubate diluted plasma samples on the coated plates for 2 hours at room temperature.
Rinse the plates with wash buffer (PBS with 0.1% Tween-20).
Dilute anti-human IgG secondary antibody labeled with HRP in dilution buffer to a concentration of 1:5000.
Incubate diluted secondary antibody on the coated plates for 20 minutes at room temperature while protecting from light.
Rinse the plates with wash buffer (PBS with 0.1% Tween-20).
Measure absorbance at 450 nm using R&D substrate as per manufacturer’s recommendation.
Seed HEK-293T cells from a stock solution.
Split cells between 70%–90% confluency.
Aspirate cell media from the flask.
Expose cells to EDTA-Trypsin for 5 min.
Add DMEM + 10% to the cell flask.
Transfer trypsinized cells, split at 5 × 10^4, into a 96 well plate.
Co-transfect HEK-293T cells using Lipofectamine 2000 with:
25 ng of an IFN-β promoter-firefly luciferase reporter plasmid
25 ng of pRL-TK Renilla luciferase reporter plasmid
125, 12.5, and 1.25 ng of the indicated viral protein expression plasmid
Mock-treat or treat cells with SeV at a concentration of 15 hemagglutination units/mL, 24 hours after transfection.
Lysate cells 18 hours post-treatment or post-infection.
Resuspend the Luciferase Assay Substrate in Luciferase Assay Buffer II.
Dilute the stock solution of Stop & Glo® 50x to 1x with Stop & Glo® Buffer.
Add 20 μL of cell lysates to a 96-well plate for analysis.
Verify that LAR II and Stop & Glo® Reagents have been warmed to 18°C–22°C before use.
Perform assays in triplicate.
Confirm viral protein expression by Western blot analysis.
Perform pre-HDX mapping.
To approximately 100 pmol of the protein of interest (2 μL), dilute 1:10 with H2O buffer (+ 18 μL).
Dilute the mixture in a ratio of 2:3 with a selected quench buffer.
Inject the quenched solution into the LC-MS apparatus for digestion, desalting, and LC-MS/MS analysis.
Digest the protein with 200 mL/min solvent A using valve position 2 for 3 min (or 3 trap column volumes).
Separate and elute the digested protein fragments by using valve position 1 and an organic gradient from solvent A to solvent B.
Include a high organic pulse at the end of the LC gradient with 100% solvent B to decrease carryover from run to run.
Process the LC-MS/MS results using Byonic and Byologic.
Optimize digestion efficiency by comparing protein coverage, peptide length, and peptide abundance.
Count the number of identified peptides for optimization purposes.
Measure redundancy as a function of the average number of overlapping peptides across all residues.
Recommend visual inspection of redundancy in the context of protein coverage.
Repeat the experiment with different quench conditions and protease columns/column orientations.
Optimize temperature, quench incubation time, and addition of other chaotropic reagents as needed.
Include RNA in the mapping experiment to confirm it does not affect digestion.
Store proteins at -80°C for long-term storage if necessary.
Add a reducing agent when the protein contains disulfide bonds during quenching.
Incubate with elevated temperature for 1-3 minutes after adding reducing agents if required.
Minimize back exchange by carefully controlling incubation conditions, especially at elevated temperatures.
Denature proteins using other chaotropic agents like guanidine HCl as needed for better digestion.
Equilibrate unbound and bound stock solutions.
Generate higher concentration stocks for both bound and unbound states.
Dilute 2 μL of stock with 18 μL D2O buffer to achieve the final protein concentration.
Prepare the unbound protein stock solution at a concentration of approximately 25 μM.
Prepare the bound protein stock solution at a concentration of approximately 25 μM with a 1:1 ratio of RNA.
To prepare the non-deuterated control, add 18 μL H2O buffer to 2 μL of the unbound protein stock on ice.
Stop HDX by adding 30 μL quench solution to the mixture.
Flash freeze the solution and store it at -80°C.
Prepare the deuterated sample for HDX labeled protein. Add 18 μL D2O buffer to 2 μL of unbound protein stock on ice, aiming for a maximized deuteration level of approximately 90% D.
Incubate the mixture at logarithmically increasing times: 4 time points (10 s, 30 s, 300 s, 3600 s).
Quench HDX by adding 30 μL quench solution to achieve a final volume of 50 μL.
Flash freeze the sample in liquid nitrogen and store it appropriately for analysis.
Repeat all steps with the bound protein stock solution using identical conditions.
Control all buffer conditions to maintain consistency in temperature, pH, and ionic strength.
Pre-equilibrate all reagents at the temperature they will be used prior to the experiment.
Inject immediately if protein aggregates upon flash freezing.
Store flash frozen HDX samples at -80°C for up to one month.
Thaw flash frozen HDX samples at 37°C for 30 seconds just before injection.
Perform LC-MS analysis of the HDX labeled protein states.

Wash sample loop with at least three volumes (e.g., 150 μL) with water/0.1% formic acid, acetonitrile + 0.1% formic acid, and again with water + 0.1% formic acid between injections to reduce carryover.
Run a blank between samples to monitor carryover extents.
Use H2O blank: mix 20 μL H2O buffer with 30 μL quench.
Use D2O blank: mix 2 μL H2O buffer, 18 μL D2O buffer, and 30 μL quench.
